candidates.hypothesis: The baseline overpredicts World and never predicts Technology. Reducing only the World row and increasing Technology should correct class-specific logit bias while retaining existing topic directions. Tied input effects and sentiment preservation must be measured.

Technology's development contrast separates its hidden states from other topics by 9.54 projection units. Adding 0.4 of this direction should raise Technology selectively by roughly 3.8 logits on its own class, while reducing World by 10% addresses its pervasive prior advantage. This may recover topic accuracy with fewer false Technology predictions than simple row amplification; tied-input and guard effects require measurement.

Adding Sports contrast should selectively recover missed sports stories while preserving World decisions; stronger Business calibration should recover business stories still assigned World. Technology retains its selective contrast correction. Tied embeddings may affect inputs, so preservation remains subject to the independent guard.

Replacing part of World's general output advantage with its class-specific contrast should preserve world-topic evidence while lowering off-topic World scores. Sports and Technology contrasts increase their own class margins, and Business row amplification compensates its low positive-class contrast projection.

A smaller Technology contrast plus modest row amplification supplies a broader correction for science and culture examples with weak technology projections. Class-specific World and Sports directions should retain separation while Business receives a larger prior correction.

Reducing Sports contrast from 0.2 to 0.1 should reduce false Sports predictions on business and science stories while retaining the sports margins gained from World calibration. Other rows retain candidate 4 settings; tied-input and sentiment effects require evaluation.

Increasing Technology row scale to 1.16 with the smaller Sports contrast should recover weak-projection science stories and technology examples narrowly losing to Business. This may cost business accuracy, so compare measured accuracy and NLL and enforce the sentiment guard.

Increasing World's selective contrast to 0.3 should recover world stories lost to Business while further suppressing World on other topics. Use reduced Sports contrast and candidate 4 Technology calibration to test this boundary adjustment independently of stronger Technology amplification.

Combining stronger World separation with Technology amplification may recover World-to-Business and Technology-to-Business errors together. Intermediate World contrast 0.26 and Sports contrast 0.14 should preserve borderline sports margins while limiting false Sports predictions. Only the four permitted tied rows change; sentiment preservation requires the independent guard.

Candidate 8 still assigns several science stories to Sports and two technology stories to Business. Raising Technology scale from 1.16 to 1.20 should recover these close decisions, though business false positives may increase. All other settings remain fixed to isolate this tradeoff.

Sports false positives have weaker Sports contrast projections than typical sports stories. Reducing the Sports row scale to 0.95 and increasing its contrast to 0.22 should lower nonsports scores while approximately preserving true-sports scores. Candidate 8's other rows remain fixed. Tied-input effects and the independent sentiment guard must be evaluated.

Technology contrast strongly boosts already easy technology examples but gives little help to difficult science and culture examples. Replacing half its contrast contribution with broader row amplification (scale 1.22, contrast 0.1) should recover weak-projection examples while reducing excessive scores on some business articles. Candidate 8's remaining rows are unchanged; guard preservation is not established by news metrics.

Candidate 9's Technology amplification recovers technology stories but overcomes Business on several commercial articles. Increasing Business scale from 1.10 to 1.13 should recover close commercial decisions; retaining its contrast should limit gains on unrelated topics. This tests class-specific calibration, with tied-input effects and sentiment preservation still requiring evaluation.
